newsitem.title: USA: House spending bill may seek $200 mln SPR oil sale.
newsitem.headline: House spending bill may seek $200 mln SPR oil sale.

text.p: A House committee is considering selling $200 million worth of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to help balance the budget, according to a letter released Monday.
The oil sale might be included in a spending bill set to be debated Tuesday by the House interior appropriations subcommittee.
House appropriations committee aides declined to comment on whether the spending bill included a $200 million oil sale, saying that the bill was still being written.

House energy and power subcommittee chairman Dan Schaefer, a Colorado Republican, who has vehemently opposed selling off SPR oil as a source of revenue over the last 18 months, said he objected to the proposed $200 million sale.

"We are writing to express our strong objections to the legislative language in the bill which, as we understand it, provides for the sale of $200,000,000 worth of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve," he said in a June 13 letter.

"Budgetary sales of oil from the reserve have already reduced our net import protection from 75 days to 67 days, considerably less than the 90 days required by the International Energy Agreement, of which the U.S. is a signatory," they said.

The government has approved the sale of nearly 30 million barrels of oil over the last two years, first to offset the costs of shutting down of a damaged SPR cavern and then to help balance the budget.
"We appreciate the difficulties of the current budget situation," the letter said. "However, a balanced budget will not be achieved by selling our energy security at bargain basement rates."
